title: soft-slot-reservation-with-decay-and-age-weighted-fairness
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Introduce a tunable soft slot reservation mechanism for the continuous batcher that reduces tail latency for small/latency-sensitive requests while preventing starvation of large/kv-heavy requests. Default off behind feature flag; safe rollout is recommended.
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching currently balances throughput vs tail latency by using hard deadlines and coarse fairness buckets. In mixed workloads (small chat turns interleaved with long KV-pinned generations) small requests see 95/99th tail spikes when batch slots are consumed by long-running work. This PR implements a soft slot reservation scheme with decay and age-weighting to reduce tail latency without starving heavy flows.

What this change does: Adds a lightweight reservation allocator that maintains ephemeral slot credits per request class (class determined by token-boundary hints + KV pin flag). Credits are granted based on recent service rate and a configurable reservation window and then decay exponentially if unused. Reservations are "soft": they bias the batch selection algorithm (probabilistic weight addition) rather than forcibly preempting existing work. To guard against starvation the scheduler applies an age-weighted fairness boost which increases priority of waiting requests over time and a fast-reclaim timer that recovers unused reservations from stalled owners after a short threshold.

Key knobs and defaults: feature flag: scheduler.enable_soft_reservations (default false) reservation_window_ms: 50 (rolling window for granting) reservation_decay_half_life_ms: 200 reclaim_threshold_ms: 150 age_boost_rate: 0.01 per 10ms max_soft_fraction: 0.25 (max fraction of batch slots influenced by reservations) preemption_safe_mode: when true, reservations never preempt already-started kernels; default true.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics: scheduler.soft_reservations_granted_total, scheduler.soft_reservations_reclaimed_total, scheduler.age_boost_factor, scheduler.reservation_usage_ratio. Added per-class latency histograms and a dedicated dashboard wiring in perf/soft-reservations.

Behavior under load: In synthetic mixed workload perf-canary runs we observed: small requests (<=64 tokens) 95th latency reduced from 122ms -> 68ms (~44% improvement) at 85% aggregate capacity; 99th reduced from 310ms -> 148ms. End-to-end throughput changed by -1.6% in a KV-heavy saturated synthetic (worst-case), but improvement for latency-sensitive classes was measured without tail amplification.

Testing and validation: unit tests for allocator and decay model added (tests/scheduler/reservation_test.go), integration tests in the continuous-batcher harness and a canary config under pkg/bench/perf_canary/elastic_reservations.yaml. We ran a 48-hour perf canary across two clusters (canary-1: small-L, canary-2: mixed-KV) to detect regressions; Canary metrics are linked in the internal dashboard (ENG-4689).

Compatibility and rollout: The feature is behind scheduler.enable_soft_reservations and off by default for no-risk installs. Rollout plan: (1) enable in perf CI and canaries, (2) enable for a subset of tenants via console feature flag for 1 week, (3) staged ramp across Dedicated pools, (4) enable-by-default after metrics stabilization. Emergency kill-switch available via scheduler.feature_toggle.

Risk and mitigations: There is a small throughput regression in synthetic KV-saturated tails; mitigations include lowering max_soft_fraction and enabling preemption_safe_mode. The implementation avoids kernel-level preemption (no in-flight kernel termination) to prevent instability on CUDA/ROCm paths.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on correctness of reclaim logic (pkg/scheduler/slot_reservations.go), interactions with KV pin prioritization (pkg/kv/cache_manager.go hooks), and telemetry labels for per-class histograms. The implementation takes care to remain lock-light and uses atomic counters to avoid contention hotspots.

Related: builds on prior work (ENG-4412 queue-horizon experiments) but differs by using probabilistic weighting and timed decay rather than strict slot leases.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (docs/perf/soft_reservations.md) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Perf canary run completed - [x] Observability wired - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Docs and release notes prepared

notes_for_ops: When enabling the feature flag in production, monitor scheduler.reservation_usage_ratio and scheduler.soft_reservations_reclaimed_total for the first 24 hours. If reclaimed rate exceeds 10% of grants for a reservation class, reduce reservation_window_ms by 50% or disable max_soft_fraction.
